number.why: The primary 3-point MACE result is saxagliptin versus placebo HR 1.00 (95% CI 0.89–1.12). Matching primary-event counts link the published estimate to the registry's ITT population and full follow-up window. The 2-year qualifier describes Kaplan–Meier percentages.

quotes.span: The primary end point was a composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or ischemic stroke.

A primary end-point event occurred in 613 patients in the saxagliptin group and in 609 patients in the placebo group (7.3% and 7.2%, respectively, according to 2-year Kaplan-Meier estimates; hazard ratio with saxagliptin, 1.00; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.89 to 1.12; P=0.99 for superiority; P<0.001 for noninferiority); the results were similar in the "on-treatment" analysis (hazard ratio, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.91 to 1.17).
TIME FRAME: Randomization (day 0) up to 2.9 years | POPULATION: Intention To Treat (ITT) analysis of randomized population. Events were adjudicated by the Clinical Event Adjudication Committee.

entry.why: The packet establishes adults with type 2 diabetes receiving a DPP-4 inhibitor versus placebo in a randomized, double-blind trial. Restriction to elevated cardiovascular risk does not contradict the question's population.

quotes.span: including saxagliptin, a dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP-4) inhibitor

We randomly assigned 16,492 patients with type 2 diabetes who had a history of, or were at risk for, cardiovascular events to receive saxagliptin or placebo and followed them for a median of 2.1 years.

A Multicentre, Randomised, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Phase IV Trial to Evaluate the Effect of Saxagliptin on the Incidence of Cardiovascular Death, Myocardial Infarction or Ischaemic Stroke in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes
ELIGIBILITY AGE/SEX: minimum age 40 Years | maximum age None | sex ALL
